newsitem.title: SPAIN: Privatisation to boost ZCCM copper, cobalt output.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation to boost ZCCM copper, cobalt output.

text.p: The privatisation of the state-owned mining giant Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) will significantly boost production of copper and cobalt, said Eckart Hilmer, a consultant to the Zambian agency in charge of privatisation.
Negotiations have begun with bidders for ZCCM's assets, and the sale of the seven mining packages and power transmission package should be concluded during the third quarter of 1997.

"Once these are completed, we expect copper production to surge from the current 330,000 tonnes per annum to around one million tonnes in another five to seven years," Hilmer told Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference on Wednesday.
Copper production has declined in Zambia in recent years, as has output of cobalt. Cobalt production is around 3,200 tonnes a year, down from levels of 4,500.
But privatisation should boost production of this metal, too, as there are high cobalt values in Konkola North and Konkola Deep that can be exploited.
"When it is in full swing, cobalt production will go up to around 6,000 or 7,000 tonnes a year," Hilmer said.
